en eksmand.explanation: "En eksmand" means "an ex-husband". It is built from "eks" (former) and "en mand" (a man or husband). To say "my husband", use "min mand": "Min mand er hjemme" (My husband is home).

en ekspedient.explanation: "En ekspedient" means "a store clerk". To say what someone does for a living, leave out "en": "Hun er ekspedient" (She is a store clerk).

en ekspedition.explanation: "En ekspedition" means "a service / transaction". When you mean a long trip to explore a place, it means "an expedition": "en ekspedition til Grønland" (an expedition to Greenland).

related.en: to handle a person at a counter

en ekspert.explanation: "En ekspert" means "an expert". To name the subject, add "i" (in): "Hun er ekspert i vin" (She is an expert in wine).

en eksplosion.explanation: "En eksplosion" means "an explosion". To say prices jump suddenly, say: "en eksplosion i priserne" (a sudden jump in prices).

en elastik.explanation: "En elastik" means "a rubber band". To say clothes have a stretchy band in them, it means "elastic": "Der er elastik i bukserne" (There is elastic in the pants).

en elbil.explanation: "En elbil" means "an electric car". It is built from "el" (electricity) and "en bil" (a car). The same "el" starts "en elcykel" (an electric bike).

en elefant.explanation: "En elefant" means "an elephant". To say someone is clumsy, use the saying "som en elefant i en porcelænsbutik" (like an elephant in a china shop).

en elektriker.explanation: "En elektriker" means "an electrician". To say what someone does for a living, leave out "en": "Min bror er elektriker" (My brother is an electrician).

en elektronikbutik.explanation: "En elektronikbutik" means "an electronics store". It is built from "elektronik" (electronics) and "en butik" (a store).

en elev.explanation: "En elev" means "a pupil". When you talk about someone learning a trade at a workplace, it means "a trainee": "Hun er elev hos en elektriker" (She is a trainee with an electrician). For university, use "en studerende" (a student): "Han er studerende" (He is a student).

en elevator.explanation: "En elevator" means "an elevator". The word "en lift" (a lift) means the same: "Liften er i stykker" (The lift is broken). To say you travel by it, use "med" (by): "Vi kører med elevatoren" (We go by the elevator).

en elg.explanation: "En elg" means "a moose / elk". Do not mix it up with "et rensdyr" (a reindeer): "Rensdyret lever i Lapland" (The reindeer lives in Lapland).

en elkedel.explanation: "En elkedel" means "an electric kettle". It is built from "el" (electricity) and "en kedel" (a kettle). The same "el" starts "en elbil" (an electric car).

en elpære.explanation: "En elpære" means "a light bulb". It is built from "el" (electricity) and "en pære" (a pear), because the bulb is shaped like one. The same "pære" is the fruit: "Jeg spiser en pære" (I eat a pear).

en elregning.explanation: "En elregning" means "an electricity bill". It is built from "el" (electricity) and "en regning" (a bill). The same "regning" is in the phrase for asking for the check: "Regningen, tak" (The check, please).

en elskerinde.explanation: "En elskerinde" means "a mistress". It comes from "at elske" (to love). The ending "-inde" marks a woman, as in "en sangerinde" (a female singer).

en embedsmand.explanation: "En embedsmand" means "a civil servant". It is built from "et embede" (a public post) and "en mand" (a man).

en emhætte.explanation: "En emhætte" means "a range hood". To tell someone to switch it on, say: "Tænd for emhætten" (Turn on the range hood).

en emission.explanation: "En emission" means "an emission". In finance it has another meaning, a company selling new shares: "en emission af aktier" (an issue of shares).

en emoji.explanation: "En emoji" means "an emoji". To say you sent one in a message, say: "Jeg sendte en glad emoji" (I sent a happy emoji).

en encyklopædi.explanation: "En encyklopædi" means "an encyclopedia". Spell it with "k" and "æ", not "c" and "ae". The word "et leksikon" (an encyclopedia) means the same: "Jeg slog det op i et leksikon" (I looked it up in an encyclopedia).

en ende.explanation: "En ende" means "an end". To say where something lies, use "i enden af" (at the end of): "Huset ligger i enden af korridoren" (The house lies at the end of the hallway). For the end of a story, use "en slutning" (an ending) instead: "Filmen har en god slutning" (The film has a good ending).

en endelse.explanation: "En endelse" means "an ending (of a word)". To see one, take "talede" (spoke): the ending is "-ede". For the end of a story, use "en slutning" (a conclusion): "Bogen har en trist slutning" (The book has a sad ending).

en endestation.explanation: "En endestation" means "a terminus / last stop". It is built from "ende" (end) and "en station" (a station). The part "ende" is also in "i enden af gaden" (at the end of the street).
